title: Put it together: this, otherwise that
idea: Wrap up the unit: the if/else shape, exactly-one-branch rule, flipping conditions, and the = vs == trap, with review.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of an if/else to its job.

pairs.right: Runs its step when the fact is true
Marks the step inside each branch

exercises.explanation: if holds the true outcome, else holds the otherwise outcome, colons end the headers, and indentation marks each branch's step.
8 > 10 is False, so the else branch runs: Small.

exercises.prompt: In an if/else, exactly one branch runs every time.
exercises.explanation: The condition is either true or false, so one branch always runs — never both, never neither.

exercises.prompt: Review the trap: which symbol does the if condition use to CHECK?
exercises.explanation: An if checks, so it uses ==. One = would store. 'One store, two ask.'

exercises.prompt:
These two versions behave the same. What makes them match?

A: if x >= 0: print("OK") else: print("Neg")
B: if x < 0: print("Neg") else: print("OK")
options: The comparison was flipped AND the branches were swapped
exercises.explanation: >= 0 flips to < 0, and the outcomes swap places too. Flip both together and the meaning stays the same.

exercises.prompt:
Review of Unit 21: a plain if (no else). What shows?

score = 20
if score > 50:
    print("High")
exercises.explanation: A one-sided if with a false condition simply skips its step. Without an else, nothing prints.

options: else must not carry a condition — just else:
Adult needs to be a number
exercises.explanation: else already means 'every other case', so it takes no condition. Write it as else:.

exercises.prompt: Arrange these into a correct if/else that prints Even check result.
exercises.explanation: if n % 2 == 0: with indented Even, then else: with indented Odd. (Review: % gives the remainder from Unit 12.)

exercises.prompt: Select EVERY true statement about if/else.
options: Both the if and else headers end with a colon
exercises.explanation: Colons on both headers, else lined up with if, exactly one branch runs. else does NOT carry a condition — that option is false.

exercises.prompt: What can you now do that you could not before this unit?
options: Choose between two outcomes with if/else, so something always happens
Handle three or more separate cases
exercises.explanation: You can write a two-outcome choice: do this, otherwise do that. Later units will add more cases and repetition.
